h: A day by the sea in Hove
p: Treat your session like a proper match day. Wear trainers, bring a light layer you can take off when you're batting, and if you're coming as a group, sort out teams before you get to the crease. Starting on an easier bowling setting and working up is the best way to keep beginners smiling, while the confident batters can ramp up the pace and see how they cope. Little ones who are new to cricket will love just hearing the crack of bat on ball.

Getting to the ground is straightforward. Hove station is a walk away, and buses run along the main roads between Brighton and Hove. On county match days the area gets much busier, so allow extra time, and remember parking near the ground can be tight.

Afterwards, head south to the seafront. Hove Lawns are a lovely open stretch beside the promenade, perfect for a picnic or a kick-about, and the walk east along the front takes you towards Brighton, with the British Airways i360 tower and the Palace Pier with its rides and arcades. Hove Museum and Art Gallery is a small but charming stop with a toy collection that's a hit with kids, and the shops, cafés and restaurants of Church Road and George Street give you plenty of choice for a bite. The North Laine area of Brighton is ideal for quirky independent shopping too.
